script: The ocean is salty mostly because of rocks on land. Rain slowly dissolves minerals from rocks, and rivers carry them to the sea. Hydrothermal vents on the sea floor add minerals too. When seawater evaporates, the salt stays behind. Seawater is about 3.5 percent salt. If all the ocean's salt were spread over the land, it could form a layer over 150 meters thick.
